questions.question: A system speaks new text in a reference person’s voice. Which task is this?
options: Speaker diarization over a meeting
Voice cloning on the TTS side
Speaker verification against an enrollment
Voice conversion on source speech
questions.explanation: Voice cloning combines new text with a reference speaker representation to synthesize new speech in that voice. Conversion changes the identity of an existing utterance while preserving its source content; cloning generates from text.

questions.question: A conversion system must preserve the source words while changing the speaker identity. What decomposition enables this?
options: Average source and target speakers into one embedding
Keep one waveform and alter its recording rate
Replace the source transcript with a target transcript
Separate content from speaker identity and recombine
questions.explanation: Conversion factors the signal into content, speaker identity, and prosody, then recombines the source content with the target speaker representation. Averaging blends identities instead of preserving the source words while substituting the target identity.

questions.question: Which voice-conversion family extracts phonetic content representations before resynthesis?
options: Disentanglement using a latent bottleneck only
Direct waveform equalization with speaker labels
Neural codec generation from text tokens alone
Recognition-synthesis using PPG-like content features
questions.explanation: Recognition-synthesis extracts content features such as phoneme posteriors or PPGs with an ASR-like model, then resynthesizes with the target speaker embedding. The “disentanglement using a latent bottleneck” option instead swaps factors inside an autoencoder representation.

questions.question: What reference condition does the lesson give for reliable F5-TTS cloning?
options: The reference transcript must match its audio exactly
A transcript is unnecessary when the clip is five seconds
The reference text should paraphrase the audio naturally
The transcript should describe the target generated sentence
questions.explanation: The F5 example conditions on a reference clip and its matching reference text; the new utterance is supplied separately as generation text. A mismatch breaks alignment between the reference transcript and speech, weakening the conditioning example.

questions.question: A cloning service accepts a signed consent record. Which pair of controls matches the documented inference path?
options: Check transcript length, then disable provenance logging
Verify consent, then embed a watermark in output
Verify speaker cosine, then remove generated metadata
Compare source noise, then store the raw waveform publicly
questions.explanation: The safe path verifies consent before synthesis and embeds a watermark in the generated waveform so provenance can be checked later. Speaker similarity shows voice match, not permission; removing the signed metadata also discards provenance instead of satisfying the documented controls.

questions.question: The toy demo’s watermark survives its direct detect step. What should you conclude about production robustness?
options: That it survives MP3 conversion and light noise
That it proves the reference speaker consented
That it resists every common audio manipulation
Only that the toy encode-detect contract worked
questions.explanation: The toy detector compares watermarked samples directly with the original waveform and recovers the injected bit pattern. No compression or noise attack occurs in the demo; its direct encode-detect check proves only the toy interface contract.
